stage_fields.biological_unit: biological_replication_unit = donor (the animal / patient the cells came from). generalization_axis = NEW donor, NOT new cell within a donor: cells from one donor are correlated (shared dissociation, library, batch, donor genotype), so for a claim that generalizes to 'this method recovers counts on a future sample' the donor is the independent replicate. Observational unit = cell. Cells are NOT biological replicates for this estimand; cell-level n is pseudoreplication at the new-donor axis (Squair et al. 2021). Note: the *method* operates cell-by-cell, but the *validity claim* (imputation reduces error on unseen samples) is judged at donor level.
stage_fields.estimand: The counterfactual true transcript count y*_{c,g} at a position (cell c, gene g) whose observed value is zero due to technical dropout (mask M_{c,g}=0), over the target population of future scRNA-seq experiments on the same tissue/platform family -- the count that would have been observed absent technical dropout. This is a per-position counterfactual count, NOT a global 'denoised matrix' summary.
stage_fields.cohort_structure: Typical scRNA-seq imputation benchmark cohort: n_donors across studies (e.g. PBMC 10x v3: 1 healthy donor, ~2.7k cells; mouse cortex: several donors; pancreas ( Baron 2016 ): ~2k cells from multiple human donors). For a NEW-donor generalization claim the usable biological n is the donor count, which is small (often 2-6); millions of cells do NOT raise the donor-level power. The method runs cell-by-cell but the evaluation of 'does imputation help unseen donors' is donor-level.
stage_fields.leakage_graph: dependency_structure: cells within a donor are correlated (shared library + dissociation); cells across donors of the same batch/study are weakly correlated; cells across studies/platforms are near-independent at the biological level but differ by technical depth/noise. leak-relevant unit for the new-donor axis = DONOR. Train/test MUST NOT share a donor. In mask-then-impute evaluation there is an additional WITHIN-cell leakage path: the mask decides which observed entries are 'held out', so the mask sampling process must be independent of expression magnitude (see split_strategy) -- an expression-coupled mask hides the MNAR failure (trap T3).
stage_fields.split_strategy: Two nested splits. (1) FOR EVALUATING IMPUTATION ERROR: hold out a random fraction (e.g. 20%) of NON-ZERO observed entries per cell as pseudo-ground-truth, mask them to zero, impute, score RMSE/Pearson on the held-out values. split_unit = entry; split_unit_justification = 'imputation error is a per-counterfactual-count claim, so the held-out unit is a single observed count treated as if it were dropped; donor-level split is irrelevant here because we are NOT generalizing to a new donor for this sub-question, we are scoring within-sample recovery.' CRITICAL: the mask is sampled independently of expression magnitude (a Bernoulli mask on observed entries, NOT a magnitude-coupled mask) -- otherwise the evaluation silently turns into MNAR and hides the failure. (2) FOR THE NEW-DONOR GENERALIZATION CLAIM: donor-level leave-out (k-fold by donor, stratified by condition) -- split_unit = donor; split_unit_justification = 'the utility claim generalizes to future donors, so the split must isolate whole donors.'
